---
title: "Introduction"
---

Neuralyzer (WhiskerToolbox) is an open-source desktop platform for neural and behavioral data analysis, developed by neuroscientists who use it every day. Its primary purpose is to act as both a reproducibility machine and a practical toolkit for data exploration.

In real experiments, it is hard to align all your data and visualize everything together. Doing this repeatedly across many concurrent data modalities can become complex and tedious. Neuralyzer is built as a workbench for behavioral and neural recordings so those multimodal workflows stay connected, time-aligned, and manageable.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- Built for neural time-series, media, spatial annotations, and derived features.
- Designed so heterogeneous data can be inspected and interacted with in one interface.
- Engineered for cross-platform scientific workflows (macOS, Linux, Windows).
:::

## What This Program Does

### Core capabilities

- **Single-place data interaction:** Keep signals, events, labels, media, and derived outputs in one connected workspace for exploration and decision-making.
- **Data ingestion and organization:** Import analog signals, digital events/intervals, tensors, points, lines, masks, and media.
- **Unified analysis workflows:** Apply transforms and feature extraction pipelines to convert raw data into interpretable outputs.
- **Interactive visualization:** Explore data through time-series views, media overlays, event plots, scatter/heatmap views, and specialized widgets.
- **Machine learning support:** Integrate supervised/unsupervised pipelines and dimensionality reduction for exploratory and predictive analysis.
- **Deep learning integration:** Run encoder/post-encoder modules and use model-aware tooling for modern feature workflows.

### Typical use cases

- Curating and triaging long recordings.
- Building reproducible processing pipelines for lab-specific modalities.
- Comparing model outputs against raw signals and labels.
- Exporting publication-ready summaries and plot-derived tables.

### Example workflow: tongue masks with optogenetic events

Suppose you want to load a video of a mouse licking a spout and also load predicted tongue masks so you can track tongue area while optogenetic stimulation is being recorded.

In Neuralyzer, you can load all of these modalities, run transforms to compute mask area, derive intervals where licking occurs, and then measure how many licks fall inside each optogenetic stimulus event. Even when TTL events were recorded on a different acquisition path and may live in a different TimeFrame, the platform is designed to make this cross-modal analysis straightforward and easy to perform in one place.

## How It Is Written

## Architecture Overview {.tabset}

### Application stack

- **Language and standard:** C++23
- **GUI framework:** Qt6
- **Build system:** CMake presets
- **Testing:** Catch2 (plus dedicated fuzz-test targets)

Speed is the primary reason the core platform is written in C++. The goal is to keep interaction responsive on large videos, high-rate neural streams, dense labels, and many concurrent modalities without sacrificing correctness or reproducibility.

The codebase is split into focused libraries, then composed into the main application. This separation keeps the UI responsive while protecting core logic from GUI coupling.

### Library design

The platform is intentionally modular. Important layers include:

- **Data core:** strongly typed temporal indexing and object storage/orchestration.
- **Processing layer:** transforms, feature extraction, and conversion pipelines.
- **Visualization layer:** plotting abstractions and backend renderers.
- **UI layer:** editor-state driven widgets and dockable tools.

This arrangement allows teams to add data types or algorithms without destabilizing unrelated modules.

### Extensibility model

WhiskerToolbox emphasizes registries and schemas:

- Parameter schemas are extracted and used to auto-generate user-facing controls.
- Processing and synthesis systems use registration patterns so new operations can be introduced cleanly.
- IO and transform ecosystems are designed to accommodate both built-in and project-specific workflows.

## General Philosophy

### Read-first, write-intentionally

The baseline posture is conservative around data mutation: inspect first, validate assumptions, and write only when the user explicitly chooses to commit/export/save. This protects source datasets and keeps analysis sessions auditable.

::: {.callout-important title="No-write-access mindset"}
The system is designed so that exploration and diagnosis can happen safely without forcing writes to canonical data. Persisting changes is an explicit step, not a side effect of simply viewing or analyzing data.
:::

### Scientific ergonomics over novelty

The interface and APIs prioritize:

- clear provenance,
- predictable transformations,
- high signal-to-noise visual feedback,
- and reproducibility under real lab constraints.

### Speed-first with clarity

The implementation targets high throughput and low-latency interaction while preserving understandable abstractions. The goal is speed that remains maintainable by research and engineering teams over time.

## Who This Is For

WhiskerToolbox is meant for people who need one environment to inspect heterogeneous data, connect manual review with algorithmic processing, and move from raw recordings to defensible results.

This includes:

- Experimental neuroscientists working with synchronized video, electrophysiology, behavior labels, and stimulation events.
- Behavioral scientists who need to annotate, curate, and quantify structure in long recordings.
- Lab engineers and analysts building reproducible pipelines that can be rerun across cohorts and sessions.
- Computational researchers who want to compare model outputs against raw data in the same interface.
- Trainees and students who benefit from a visual, end-to-end workflow instead of stitching together many scripts and tools.

If your workflow spans media, labels, events, intervals, analog traces, and derived features, this platform is built for that intersection.
